q0.t: Question 1. My sister, blank, the piano every afternoon.

q0_a0.t: My sister plays the piano every afternoon.

q0_a1.t: My sister play the piano every afternoon.

q0_a2.t: My sister is playing the piano every afternoon.

q0_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: plays. It's a routine, and my sister is third person, so we use the present simple with an s: plays.

q0_ok.t: Correct! It's a routine, and my sister is third person, so we use the present simple with an s: plays.

q1.t: Question 2. Listen! The neighbours, blank, again.

q1_a1.t: Listen! The neighbours are arguing again.

q1_a2.t: Listen! The neighbours have argued again.

q1_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: are arguing. Listen! tells us it's happening right now, so we use the present continuous.

q1_ok.t: Correct! Listen! tells us it's happening right now, so we use the present continuous.

q2.t: Question 3. I, blank, him at the party last Saturday.

q2_a0.t: I have seen him at the party last Saturday.

q2_a1.t: I see him at the party last Saturday.

q2_a2.t: I saw him at the party last Saturday.

q2_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: saw. Last Saturday is a finished time, so we use the past simple, not the present perfect.

q2_ok.t: Correct! Last Saturday is a finished time, so we use the past simple, not the present perfect.

q3.t: Question 4. I, blank, English for six years.

q3_a0.t: I am studying English for six years.

q3_a1.t: I have been studying English for six years.

q3_a2.t: I study English for six years.

q3_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: have been studying. It's the duration of an activity with for, so we use have been, plus -ing.

q3_ok.t: Correct! It's the duration of an activity with for, so we use have been, plus -ing.

q4.t: Question 5. I, blank, her since we were at school.

q4_a0.t: I have been knowing her since we were at school.

q4_a1.t: I am knowing her since we were at school.

q4_a2.t: I have known her since we were at school.

q4_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: have known. Know is a state verb, so it never goes in the continuous: I have known her.

q4_ok.t: Correct! Know is a state verb, so it never goes in the continuous: I have known her.

q5.t: Question 6. The shop, blank, yet. We'll have to wait.

q5_a0.t: The shop hasn't opened yet. We'll have to wait.

q5_a1.t: The shop doesn't open yet. We'll have to wait.

q5_a2.t: The shop isn't opening yet. We'll have to wait.

q5_no.t: Not quite. The right answer is: hasn't opened. Yet goes with the present perfect: the shop hasn't opened yet.

q5_ok.t: Correct! Yet goes with the present perfect: the shop hasn't opened yet.

s0_0_0.t: Hello, and welcome to Present Lab!

s0_1_0.t: This educational app has been made by Nuria Calvo, an English teacher at IES Goya, Zaragoza.

s0_2_0.t: In English, there are four present tenses, and each one tells us something different.

s0_2_1.t: S: [surprised] Four? I thought there was only one present!

s0_2_2.t: [firm, smiling] Four! And by the end of this lesson, you'll know them all.

s0_3_0.t: Today you'll learn the present simple, the present continuous, the present perfect and the present perfect continuous. And how to choose the right one!

s1_1_0.t: We use it for routines, habits, general truths, timetables and states.

s1_1_1.t: S: [trying it out] Like... I get up at seven every day?

s1_1_2.t: Exactly! And water freezes at zero degrees.

s1_2_0.t: Watch out for he, she and it: the verb takes an s.

s1_2_1.t: S: [confident, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] My sister play the piano.

s1_2_2.t: [firm, correcting at once] No! My sister plays. Add the s!

s1_2_3.t: S: [repeating carefully] My sister plays the piano.

s1_3_0.t: In negatives and questions, we use do and does.

s1_3_1.t: S: [unsure, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] Tom doesn't likes coffee.

s1_3_2.t: [firm] Careful! After doesn't, no s: Tom doesn't like coffee. And in questions: does she live here?

s1_4_0.t: Words like always, usually and never go before the verb, but after be.

s1_4_1.t: S: [trying it out] I always read at night. And she is never late!

s2_1_0.t: The form is: am, is or are, plus a verb ending in -ing.

s2_1_1.t: S: [checking] I'm working, she's working, they're working?

s2_2_0.t: We use it for actions happening right now, at this moment.

s2_2_1.t: S: [pointing out of the window] Look! It's raining!

s2_3_0.t: And for temporary situations: things happening these days, but not exactly now.

s2_3_1.t: S: [casual] I'm reading a great book these days.

s2_4_0.t: We also use it for fixed plans in the future, and for changes in progress.

s2_4_1.t: S: [excited] We're flying to Rome on Friday!

s2_4_2.t: And the weather is getting warmer!

s2_5_0.t: S: [confident, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] She working now.

s2_5_1.t: [firm, stopping the student] Stop! Don't forget the verb be. She is working.

s3_1_0.t: The form is: have or has, plus the past participle. It connects the past with the present, and we never say when.

s3_1_1.t: S: [checking] I have seen, she has seen?

s3_2_0.t: We use it for life experiences, often with ever and never.

s3_2_1.t: S: [curious] Have you ever eaten sushi?

s3_3_0.t: We also use it for a result we can see now, and with just, for something that has just happened.

s3_3_1.t: S: [panicking] Oh no! I've lost my keys!

s3_3_2.t: [calm] Don't panic. Your mum has just arrived.

s3_4_0.t: And for situations up to now, with for and since. For a period of time, since a starting point.

s3_4_1.t: S: [thinking it through] We've lived here for ten years. And I've known her since 2019.

s3_5_0.t: Been or gone? He has been to Paris: he went and came back. He has gone to Paris: he's still there.

s3_5_1.t: S: [understanding] So my brother has gone to the shops. He isn't here!

s3_6_0.t: S: [confident, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] I have seen him yesterday.

s3_6_1.t: [firm] No! With a finished time, like yesterday or last week, never use the present perfect. Say: I saw him yesterday.

s3_6_2.t: S: [repeating carefully] I saw him yesterday.

s4_0_0.t: Chapter four: the present perfect continuous!

s4_1_0.t: The form is: have or has, plus been, plus a verb ending in -ing. It tells us how long an activity has been going on.

s4_1_1.t: S: [proud] I've been studying English for six years!

s4_1_2.t: [impressed] Great! For, since and how long are the clues.

s4_2_0.t: We also use it for a recent activity with a visible effect.

s4_2_1.t: S: [surprised] Your hands are dirty! What have you been doing?

s4_3_0.t: But if there's a quantity, use the present perfect simple.

s4_3_1.t: S: [confident, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] We have been writing five emails.

s4_3_2.t: [firm] No! There's a quantity, five emails. Say: we have written five emails.

s4_4_0.t: And state verbs like know, like or want never go in the continuous.

s4_4_1.t: S: [unsure, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] I have been knowing her for years.

s4_4_2.t: [firm] Careful! I have known her for years.

s5_1_0.t: S: [confused] Simple, continuous, perfect... I always mix them up!

s5_1_1.t: [energetic] Here's the trick: look at the time words.

s5_2_0.t: Every day, usually and never take the present simple. Now, at the moment and look take the present continuous.

s5_2_1.t: S: [trying it out] I usually get up at seven, but this week I'm getting up at nine!

s5_3_0.t: Ever, already, yet and just take the present perfect. How long, for and since with an activity take the present perfect continuous.

s5_3_1.t: S: [thinking] We've seen this film before. And it's been raining since Monday.

s5_4_0.t: And yesterday, last week or ago? None of the presents: that's the past simple!

s5_4_1.t: S: [surprised] So: I visited my gran last weekend.

s5_5_0.t: And remember: state verbs, like like, know and want, stay simple.

s5_5_1.t: S: [confident, mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] She isn't liking chocolate.

s5_5_2.t: [firm] Not quite! She doesn't like chocolate, but she's eating a piece right now.

s6_0_0.t: Chapter six: the top five mistakes. Let's check them one by one!

s6_1_0.t: Mistake number one: forgetting the s.

s6_1_1.t: S: [mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] He work in a bank.

s6_1_2.t: [firm] He works! He, she, it: add the s.

s6_2_0.t: Mistake number two: forgetting be in the continuous.

s6_2_1.t: S: [mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] They playing football now.

s6_2_2.t: [firm] They are playing! Am, is or are, always.

s6_3_0.t: Mistake number three: state verbs in the continuous.

s6_3_1.t: S: [mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] I am wanting a new phone.

s6_3_2.t: [firm] No! I want a new phone.

s6_4_0.t: Mistake number four: the past instead of the participle after have.

s6_4_1.t: S: [mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] I have saw that film.

s6_4_2.t: [firm] I have seen that film. Have, plus the past participle!

s6_5_0.t: And mistake number five: a hidden yesterday.

s6_5_1.t: S: [mistake: say it EXACTLY as written, word for word, keeping the grammar mistake] I have gone to the cinema yesterday.

s6_5_2.t: [firm] Yesterday is finished! I went to the cinema yesterday.

s6_5_3.t: S: [proud] Got it! No more mistakes!

s7_0_0.t: Time for a challenge! Choose the right tense for each sentence.

s8_1_0.t: Now you know the four present tenses: the present simple, the present continuous, the present perfect and the present perfect continuous.

s8_2_0.t: This educational app was made by Nuria Calvo, an English teacher at IES Goya, Zaragoza. Now it's your turn: click the button and practise with the exercises.

s8_2_1.t: S: [cheerful, waving goodbye] See you in class!
